A1.justification: Both 32-page PDFs describe the same BRO/Logit Annealing work and contain Appendices A–E. Their text, equations, tables and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy, robustness, runtime and ablation results for BRO and Logit Annealing in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including evaluations on CIFAR-10/100, Tiny-ImageNet and ImageNet.

M1.justification: The BRO parameterization, Algorithm 1, LA loss and network architectures are unchanged. The LLN head discussed in the revised Appendix B.2 was already present in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four image-classification datasets, diffusion-generated augmentation data, and certified and empirical robustness scenarios, including the appendix evaluations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the matched experiments, including SOC, LOT, Cayley, LiResNet and the additional Lipschitz and certification baselines in the appendix tables.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model configurations, augmentation settings and attack budgets are retained. Appendix B.2 newly specifies the certification bound used with the existing LLN head; it documents an existing experiment rather than reporting a protocol replacement.

E4.justification: The backbone, loss, rank and hyperparameter ablations, AutoAttack evaluations, margin analyses and LOT instability analysis are unchanged in Section 6 and Appendices A, C and D.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging three runs in Appendix B.5 and ten iterations for Figures 5–6. No run-count, seed, uncertainty-reporting or statistical-estimation practice changes.

E6.justification: All reported numerical results and plotted findings are retained. For example, Table 1 reports the same 81.6% clean accuracy and 70.6% certified accuracy at epsilon 36/255 for BRONet-L(+LA) on CIFAR-10.

T1.justification: The propositions, theorem, mathematical definitions and proofs in the main text and Appendices A and C are unchanged. Appendix A.3 receives grammatical corrections; the LLN note introduces no new mathematical definition or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about BRO efficiency, LA margin learning and certified robustness.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and Appendix E's limitations are unchanged, including inconsistent gains at larger perturbations, LA tuning requirements, the focus on l2 certification and substantial training costs.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 now explicitly states that certification uses the LLN bound instead of M_f(x)/(sqrt(2)L), with a citation to Singla et al. (2022). v1 already described the LLN head but omitted this certification detail. Other implementation information and the code link are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. The added LLN citation repeats Singla et al. (2022), already credited for the final layer in Appendix B.2; bibliography edits correct capitalization.

P1.justification: v2 corrects grammar in Appendix A.3, revises the short head description in B.2 and standardizes capitalization in references. The narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Reference corrections cause limited line wrapping and spacing changes on pages 10–12, with small local appendix text reflow. All figures and tables retain their content, design and placement.

improvement.justification: The clarification in Appendix B.2 reduces ambiguity about how certified accuracies were obtained: v1 identified the LLN head but supplied only the general certification formula. This improves reproducibility documentation, alongside small copyedits, while the methods, evidence and claims remain unchanged.
